items.question: Antidote for warfarin overdose is?
items.explanation: Vitamin K reverses warfarin (a vitamin K antagonist). Protamine reverses heparin.

items.question: Which drug precipitates thyroid storm if stopped and treats tremor in hyperthyroidism?
items.explanation: Propranolol controls adrenergic symptoms of thyrotoxicosis and blocks peripheral T4 to T3 conversion at high doses.

items.question: Which anticoagulant is preferred in antiphospholipid syndrome?
items.explanation: Warfarin is preferred in antiphospholipid syndrome; DOACs showed higher thrombosis rates in trials.

items.question: Which drug is uricosuric (increases uric acid excretion)?
items.explanation: Probenecid increases renal uric acid excretion for chronic gout. Allopurinol and febuxostat reduce uric acid production.

items.question: mRNA vaccine technology works by?
items.explanation: mRNA vaccines deliver mRNA (in lipid nanoparticles) that instructs host cells to make an antigen, triggering immunity.

*PharmaCraft Daily - 25 Oct 2026*

🎓 *MBBS* (Blood)
Q: Antidote for warfarin overdose is?
Ans: Vitamin K
Why: Vitamin K reverses warfarin (a vitamin K antagonist). Protamine reverses heparin.

🩺 *NEET PG* (Autonomic Nervous System)
Q: Which drug precipitates thyroid storm if stopped and treats tremor in hyperthyroidism?
Ans: Propranolol
Why: Propranolol controls adrenergic symptoms of thyrotoxicosis and blocks peripheral T4 to T3 conversion at high doses.

🏥 *INI-CET* (Cardiovascular)
Q: Which anticoagulant is preferred in antiphospholipid syndrome?
Ans: Warfarin
Why: Warfarin is preferred in antiphospholipid syndrome; DOACs showed higher thrombosis rates in trials.

🌍 *FMGE* (Autacoids and NSAIDs)
Q: Which drug is uricosuric (increases uric acid excretion)?
Ans: Probenecid
Why: Probenecid increases renal uric acid excretion for chronic gout. Allopurinol and febuxostat reduce uric acid production.

🔬 *MD Pharmacology* (Recent Advances)
Q: mRNA vaccine technology works by?
Ans: Delivering mRNA encoding an antigen
Why: mRNA vaccines deliver mRNA (in lipid nanoparticles) that instructs host cells to make an antigen, triggering immunity.
